newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia May industrial index up 11.4 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia May industrial index up 11.4 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Malaysia's industrial production index rose 11.4 percent year-on-year in May, the Statistics Department said on Saturday.
The index rose 2.2 percent to 158.9 from 155.5 in April, the department said. The index for the first five months of 1997 has
increased 11.3 percent to 150.8 from 135.5 recorded in the
All three divisions in the industrial sector showed increases in the first five months of this year compared with the same period in the previous year, the department said.
Mining rose 1.6 percent, manufacturing 13.4 percent and electricity 16.4 percent.
Natural gas, which rose 15.4 percent, was the main contributor to mining's increase. The indices for crude oil and tin dropped 2.3 percent and 7.3 percent respectively.
In the manufacturing division, 20 of the 23 major groups recorded higher indices for the first five months of 1997.
Plastic products registered the biggest leap of 50.2 percent, followed by non-ferrous metal basis industries which rose 33.3 percent.

Industrial chemicals gained 19.9 percent, non-metallic mineral products added 17.2 percent, electrical machinery, apparatus, appliances and supplies was up 15.1 percent, while miscellaneous products of petroleum and coal rose 14.3 percent.
Tobacco manufactures increased 14.2, textiles was up 12.4 percent and fabricated metal products, except machinery and electrical, rose 12.3 percent.
Crude oil refineries rose 11.9 percent, iron and steel basic industries increased 11.2 percent, transport equipment was up 11.1 percent and glass and glass products gained 11 percent.

The three major groups that registered declines in the first five months were footwear which decelerated 4.6 percent, beverage industries dropped which fell 2.4 percent and wearing apparel which slipped 0.4 percent.
